extended_scope: The repeated local equation for the primed divisor, immediately after the reported unprimed formula
proof: The local ring map O_{X,p} -> O_{X',p'} induced by g sends x_i to x'_i. For a prime q of the target, the inverse-image prime contains product_i x_i exactly when q contains product_i x'_i. Hence the inverse image of V(product_i x_i) is V(product_i x'_i). The ensuing localization B'[1/x'_1,...,1/x'_r] is isomorphic over B' to B'[1/(product_i x'_i)]: the first map sends 1/(product_i x'_i) to product_i (1/x'_i), and the inverse map sends 1/x'_i to (product_{j != i} x'_j)/(product_j x'_j). Both composites fix B' and the displayed generators, so they are identities.
